agency_full: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (lead) — DLR + CNES (MASCOT lander) + NASA (DSN tracking, sample-curation partnership)
payload: 609 kg dry, ion-electric propulsion (4×μ10 thrusters) + chemical bipropellant + 1.6 m HGA. Onboard payload — Small Carry-on Impactor (SCI, 2.5 kg shaped charge), MASCOT lander (10 kg, DLR/CNES), 3× MINERVA-II rovers (~1 kg each), sample return capsule (16 kg, parachute reentry).
credit: © JAXA / Hayabusa2 mission. Hayabusa2 launched 2014-12-03 from Tanegashima on a 3.5-year low-thrust ion-engine cruise to near-Earth asteroid (162173) Ryugu, with an Earth gravity assist on 2015-12-03 to phase the rendezvous. Arrival 2018-06-27 at 20 km hover distance. Surface operations 2018-2019 returned the first sustained close-up survey of a rubble-pile C-type asteroid (~1 km diameter, ~1.27 g/cm³ bulk density — implying ~50% porosity). Two touchdown-and-go sample collections (TD1 2019-02-22, TD2 2019-07-11) bracketed the SCI experiment (2019-04-05) which detonated a 2.5 kg copper-lined shaped charge to excavate a 14 m crater and expose fresh subsurface material for the second sample. The DLR/CNES MASCOT lander operated for 17 hours on the surface, and three MINERVA-II hoppers returned the first surface images from an asteroid. Sample-return capsule reentry over Woomera, Australia 2020-12-05 delivered 5.4 g of pristine Ryugu material — the first asteroid sample with subsurface stratigraphy. The Hayabusa2 mothership departed for an extended mission: flyby of (98943) 2001 CC21 in 2026-07, then rendezvous with rapidly-rotating (1998 KY26) targeted for 2031-07.
